sentences.text: The name Siroccopteryx moroccensis translates to 'wing of the Sirocco,' referencing the North African wind and the location where the animal was found.
This pterosaur possessed a long, narrow muzzle featuring a large terminal part and an anterior keel crest that stood higher than that of Anhanguera but lower than Coloborhynchus or Tropeognathus.
Its teeth were sharp and short, appearing more robust than those found in Anhanguera.
Siroccopteryx had an estimated wingspan of 4 to 5 meters.

The fossil bone surface is rough and leathery with wrinkles and depressions; while some suggest these indicate disease, researcher André Veldmeijer proposes they likely indicate a keratinous cover on the ridge.
The genus was named and described in 1999 by paleontologists Bryn Mader and Alexander Kellner.
The holotype fossil, catalogued as LINHM 016, was discovered in southeastern Morocco within red sandstone layers.
The original describers placed Siroccopteryx in the family Anhangueridae, classifying it as an extinct anhanguerid pterodactyloid pterosaur.
However, some researchers classify the animal as a member of the family Ornithocheiridae.
Siroccopteryx lived in Morocco during the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 105 million years ago.
David M. Unwin has considered Siroccopteryx to be a junior synonym of the genus Coloborhynchus, a view he suggested in 2001 that remains controversial.

A 2018 study by Longrich et al. assigned Siroccopteryx to the family Ornithocheiridae as the sister taxon of Coloborhynchus, whereas a 2019 analysis by Jacobs et al. placed it in Ornithocheiridae as a sister taxon to Ornithocheirus and Tropeognathus.
Conversely, a 2020 study by Holgado and Pêgas recovered Siroccopteryx as the sister taxon to Tropeognathus but assigned both to the family Anhangueridae.
In 2009, Kellner suggested that Siroccopteryx, Coloborhynchus clavirostris, and Uktenadactylus formed a clade within Anhangueridae.
